sentences.zh: 他确实在那方面变得臃肿了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And he's saying, not only has Luther become fat, but he's become everything that he'd previously hated, that he's become a Pope.
sentences.zh: 他说，路德不仅变胖了，而且变成了他以前所憎恨的一切，他变成了一个教皇。

sentences.en: You know, we said that he calls him a monk, calls him ambassador of the devil, and very, very painfully for Luther, accuses him of misunderstanding scripture.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们说过他称他为修士，称他为魔鬼的使者，而且对路德来说非常、非常痛苦的是，指责他误解了《圣经》。

sentences.en: Says that he's a man who has made a mockery and an utterly useless babble out of the divine word, which of course is the precise opposite of what Luther thinks.
sentences.zh: 说他是一个把神圣的话语变成嘲弄和完全无用的胡言乱语的人，这当然与路德的想法完全相反。

sentences.en: And Munzer basically is casting
sentences.zh: 闵采尔基本上是在把

sentences.en: Wittenberg as a kind of parallel of Rome.
sentences.zh: 维滕贝格描绘成罗马的翻版。

sentences.en: What is it?
sentences.zh: 那是什么？

sentences.en: Two cheeks of the same arse is the phrase.
sentences.zh: “同一个屁股的两瓣脸”，就是这句话。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, it's not what that depicts, but we can go with that phrase if you like.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那并不是那个词所描绘的意思，但如果你喜欢，我们可以用那个短语。

sentences.en: But it's very, very Munzer friendly, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 但这非常符合闵采尔的风格，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, I could absolutely imagine that he would have said that.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我完全可以想象他会那样说。

sentences.en: It's very Munzer friendly.
sentences.zh: 这非常符合闵采尔的风格。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so it's because of this, the fact that you have now Rome and Wittenberg, and both of them are Babylon, that this is why he thinks that the end times are approaching.
sentences.zh: 所以正是因为这个，因为你现在有了罗马和维滕贝格，而且它们都是巴比伦，这就是为什么他认为末日即将来临。

sentences.en: And it's why once he's been expelled by the Dukes of Saxony, he goes to Mulhersen,
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么一旦他被萨克森公爵驱逐，他就去了米尔豪森（Mulhersen），

sentences.en: and he kind of says, you know, you are the elect.
sentences.zh: 他基本上说，你知道，你们是选民。

sentences.en: This is why he does his great white flag with his rainbow and recruits his devout Christians to follow him.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么他制作了那面带有彩虹的大白旗，并招募虔诚的基督徒追随他。

sentences.en: And it's a holy war.
sentences.zh: 这是一场圣战。

sentences.en: And how he comes in May 1525 to be marching against the local princes towards the town of Frankenhausen.
sentences.zh: 这就是他在1525年5月如何向当地诸侯进军，前往弗兰肯豪森（Frankenhausen）镇的。

sentences.en: So Tom, I was just thinking, how could they have let this get to this crazy situation where this bloke, you know, ranting and raving, has raised an army.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我刚才在想，他们怎么会任由事态发展到如此疯狂的地步，让这个家伙，你知道的，在那儿大吵大闹，竟然还拉起了一支军队。

sentences.en: And actually you said he goes to Mulhersen in February 1525.
sentences.zh: 而且你刚才提到，他在1525年2月去了米尔豪森。

sentences.en: And there's an obvious reason why it's got to this point, because the emperor in February 1525 is off in Italy fighting a gigantic battle against the French, the Battle of Pavia,
sentences.zh: 事情发展到这一步是有明显原因的，因为1525年2月时，皇帝正在意大利与法国进行一场巨大的战役，即帕维亚之战，

sentences.en: where he captures the French king.
sentences.zh: 在那场战役中，他俘虏了法国国王。

sentences.en: So the emperor, Charles V, is completely distracted.
sentences.zh: 所以皇帝查理五世当时完全分身乏术。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: He's off fighting this titanic war against the French.
sentences.zh: 他当时正忙着与法国人进行那场史诗般的战争。

sentences.en: And in his backyard, you know, it's just all completely fallen apart.
sentences.zh: 而在他的后院，你知道的，一切都彻底乱套了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And that's why Luther is still alive.
sentences.zh: 这就是路德至今还活着的原因。

sentences.en: If Charles had been undistracted by all his other responsibilities as king of Spain and, you know, invading Italy and worrying about the Turks and so
sentences.zh: 如果查理没有被他作为西班牙国王的其他职责所牵制，比如入侵意大利、担心土耳其人等等，

sentences.en: on, then he could have launched a campaign, invaded Wittenberg, killed Luther, wiped the
sentences.zh: 那么他本可以发动一场战役，入侵维滕贝格，杀掉路德，彻底铲除

sentences.en: Reformation out.
sentences.zh: 宗教改革。

sentences.en: But he doesn't because he has so many distractions.
sentences.zh: 但他没这么做，因为他要操心的事情太多了。

sentences.en: And that means that it's down to the local princes to sort it out.
sentences.zh: 这意味着只能由当地的诸侯来解决这个问题。

sentences.en: And when Munzer hears who is leading the princely armies against him, it confirms him in all his contempt and hatred for the princes as representatives
sentences.zh: 当闵采尔听说领兵讨伐他的诸侯是谁时，这更加深了他对这些诸侯的蔑视和仇恨，因为他们是

sentences.en: of AntichriSt. Because we mentioned how one of the princes is the Catholic, brother of Frederick, the elector of Saxony.
sentences.zh: 敌基督的代表。因为我们提到过，其中一位诸侯是萨克森选侯弗里德里希的弟弟，一位天主教徒。

sentences.en: Oh yeah, George, Georg.
sentences.zh: 哦，对了，乔治，格奥尔格。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But the other one, Dominic, is Philip of Hesse, who has recently been converted by
sentences.zh: 但另一位，多米尼克，是黑森的腓力，他最近刚被

sentences.en: Philip Melanchthon to Lutheranism.
sentences.zh: 菲利普·梅兰希通感化，皈依了路德宗。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So there they are.
sentences.zh: 所以情况就是这样。

sentences.en: It's a Catholic and a Lutheran prince facing him.
sentences.zh: 站在他对立面的是一位天主教诸侯和一位路德宗诸侯。

sentences.en: So unsurprisingly, on the eve of the battle, Munzer goes all in, you know, his men are angels of light.
sentences.zh: 所以不出所料，在战役前夕，闵采尔孤注一掷，你知道的，他宣称他的人是光明之子。

sentences.en: The enemies are the devil.
sentences.zh: 敌人则是魔鬼。

sentences.en: He rides around the camp, telling them to trust in God, promising them that the shot of their enemies will have no power to harm them.
sentences.zh: 他在营地里骑马巡视，告诉他们要相信上帝，承诺他们敌人的炮火无法伤害他们分毫。

sentences.en: And Dominic, this does not turn out to be the case.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，事实证明并非如此。

sentences.en: I mean, he's got a big army, Tom, 8,000 people or so.
sentences.zh: 我是说，汤姆，他有一支庞大的军队，大约8000人。

sentences.en: I mean, this is not a punch up in a back alley kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 这可不是什么小巷里的斗殴。

sentences.en: But it kind of is because the word of God does not really help them because they've only got bill hooks and whatever.
sentences.zh: 但某种程度上确实是，因为上帝的旨意并没有真正帮助他们，毕竟他们手里只有草叉之类的农具。

sentences.en: Oh, right, right.
sentences.zh: 哦，对，对。

sentences.en: And they're against trained men who have been raised to fight and kill.
sentences.zh: 而且他们的对手是受过训练、以杀戮为业的职业军人。

sentences.en: They just get slaughtered.
sentences.zh: 他们简直是被屠杀。

sentences.en: And pretty much all of the people in Frankhausen are either slaughtered or taken prisoner.
sentences.zh: 弗兰肯豪森几乎所有的人要么被屠杀，要么被俘虏。

sentences.en: And when some of the women go to the princes after the battle, I mean, calling it a battle is excessive
sentences.zh: 当一些妇女在战后——我是说，把这称为战役都太抬举了——

sentences.en: after the massacre and say, you know, could we have our men who are captive back?
sentences.zh: 在屠杀之后去找诸侯，说，你知道的，能不能把我们被俘的男人还给我们？

sentences.en: The princes say, okay, you can, provided that you put to death two of the rebel priests who we've captured.
sentences.zh: 诸侯们说，可以，前提是你们要处死我们抓到的那两个叛军牧师。

sentences.en: It's your responsibility to kill them.
sentences.zh: 杀掉他们是你们的责任。

sentences.en: And I think it's a measure of the kind of the horror and the madness of the times that the women reach for cudgels and start smacking the priests, smashing their bones,
sentences.zh: 我认为，那个时代的恐怖和疯狂程度从这件事可见一斑：这些妇女拿起棍棒开始殴打那些牧师，打碎他们的骨头，

sentences.en: cracking their skulls.
sentences.zh: 敲碎他们的头骨。

sentences.en: And it is said that they keep smashing and beating them for half an hour after they've died until they're just a kind of bloody pulp.
sentences.zh: 据说在他们死后，她们还继续砸打了一个小时，直到他们变成了一滩血肉模糊的烂泥。

sentences.en: So, Tom, do you want a brilliant fact about the Battle of Frankhausen?
sentences.zh: 那么，汤姆，你想听一个关于弗兰肯豪森战役的精彩事实吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, please.
sentences.zh: 好啊，请讲。

sentences.en: Great.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: So the Battle of Frankhausen is the subject of the world's largest painting.
sentences.zh: 弗兰肯豪森战役是世界上最大的一幅油画的主题。

sentences.en: Is it?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: And this was commissioned by our old friends, the leaders of East Germany in the late 1970s.
sentences.zh: 这是我们老朋友，也就是20世纪70年代末东德的领导人们委托创作的。

sentences.en: It is in Bad Frankenhausen in the Panorama Museum.
sentences.zh: 它现在位于巴特弗兰肯豪森的全景博物馆里。

sentences.en: And it shows the Battle of Frankenhausen, but can you guess what they would call it?
sentences.zh: 它描绘了弗兰肯豪森战役，但你能猜到他们把它叫什么吗？

sentences.en: The rising of the proletariat against the evil capitalists or something.
sentences.zh: 无产阶级反抗邪恶资本家的起义之类的？

sentences.en: Pretty good.
sentences.zh: 猜得不错。

sentences.en: It's actually called the early bourgeois revolution in Germany.
sentences.zh: 它实际上叫《德国早期资产阶级革命》。

sentences.en: Brilliant.
sentences.zh: 太精彩了。

sentences.en: And I'll tell you how big it is.
sentences.zh: 我告诉你它有多大。

sentences.en: It is 46 feet by 404 feet.
sentences.zh: 它有46英尺高，404英尺长。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: That is big.
sentences.zh: 那可真够大的。

sentences.en: So it's a bloody big painting.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一幅巨大的血腥画作。

sentences.en: And is it kind of like, where's Wally?
sentences.zh: 那它是不是有点像《威利在哪里》那种风格？

sentences.en: Can you see where Munzer is?
sentences.zh: 你能找到闵采尔在哪里吗？

sentences.en: Because Munzer is found hiding in an attic after the battle.
sentences.zh: 因为闵采尔在战后被发现躲在阁楼里。

sentences.en: It's got 3,000 people.
sentences.zh: 画里有3000个人物。

sentences.en: So it must have Munzer.
sentences.zh: 所以肯定有闵采尔。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: He's supposed to be there somewhere.
sentences.zh: 他应该就在某处。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So he gets found hiding in an attic.
sentences.zh: 所以他被发现躲在阁楼里。

sentences.en: He gets dragged out.
sentences.zh: 他被拖了出来。

sentences.en: He says he's had nothing to do with it.
sentences.zh: 他说这事儿跟他没关系。

sentences.en: He's completely innocent.
sentences.zh: 他是完全无辜的。

sentences.en: And then they look through his bag and they find basically, I am Thomas Munzer, you know, all over it.
sentences.zh: 然后他们搜查了他的包，发现里面基本上全是“我是托马斯·闵采尔”之类的东西。

sentences.en: So he gets dragged in front of
sentences.zh: 于是他被拖到了

sentences.en: Duke George of Saxony.
sentences.zh: 萨克森公爵乔治面前。

sentences.en: Munzer is unapologetic.
sentences.zh: 闵采尔毫无悔意。

sentences.en: You know, he uses the incorrectly respectful form of view to George.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他用了对乔治不敬的称呼方式。

sentences.en: Oh, he misuse him.
sentences.zh: 哦，他冒犯了他。

sentences.en: He misclasses him again.
sentences.zh: 他又一次搞错了身份等级。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: He justifies the war.
sentences.zh: 他为这场战争辩护。

sentences.en: He's endlessly quoting the Bible.
sentences.zh: 他不断地引用《圣经》。

sentences.en: And so the Duke puts him to torture.
sentences.zh: 于是公爵对他动了刑。

sentences.en: There are stories that he recounts his views, but there's no evidence for this whatsoever in his public statements after this.
sentences.zh: 有传言说他撤回了自己的观点，但在他此后的公开声明中，没有任何证据支持这一点。

sentences.en: He remains completely defiant.
sentences.zh: 他始终保持着完全的反抗姿态。

sentences.en: And he's handed over to the Count of Mansfeld.
sentences.zh: 他被移交给了曼斯费尔德伯爵。

sentences.en: And Mansfeld Dominic, you may remember, is the place where Luther had grown up.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，你可能还记得，曼斯费尔德是路德成长的地方。

sentences.en: And the Count of
sentences.zh: 曼斯费尔德伯爵

sentences.en: Mansfeld takes Munzer back to Mulhausen, where he had, you know, proclaimed that he was the prophet of the end times.
sentences.zh: 把闵采尔带回了米尔豪森，也就是他曾经宣称自己是末日先知的地方。

sentences.en: He's beheaded outside its walls and his head is put on a spike and his body is put on public display to serve as a warning and a terror.
sentences.zh: 他在城墙外被斩首，头颅被插在长矛上，尸体被公开展示，以起到警示和威慑的作用。

sentences.en: So that thing about serving as a warning and a terror.
sentences.zh: 关于那种警示和威慑的作用，

sentences.en: There are some historians, aren't there, who say that effectively Munzer was not as important as we now think, and that Luther and Luther's allies inflated him.
sentences.zh: 有些历史学家认为，闵采尔实际上并没有我们现在认为的那么重要，是路德和路德的盟友夸大了他。

sentences.en: They deliberately exaggerated his importance because they wanted to create a bogeyman and to frighten people away from radicalism and back towards conservatism.
sentences.zh: 他们故意夸大他的重要性，因为他们想制造一个“妖怪”，把人们从激进主义中吓跑，拉回到保守主义阵营。

sentences.en: In other words, they were doing exactly the same as what people did in 1650s England with, let's say,
sentences.zh: 换句话说，他们所做的和1650年代英国人对待，比如说，

sentences.en: the ranters, who maybe didn't even exiSt. And that actually Munzer was a more marginal and bonkers figure.
sentences.zh: “狂乱者”（Ranters）的做法如出一辙，那些人甚至可能根本不存在。实际上，闵采尔是一个更边缘、更疯狂的人物。

sentences.en: Munzer is definitely a marginal figure.
sentences.zh: 闵采尔绝对是一个边缘人物。

sentences.en: I mean, the Peasants' War does not happen because of Munzer.
sentences.zh: 我是说，农民战争并不是因为闵采尔才发生的。

sentences.en: Munzer is piggybacking onto the Peasants' Rebellion.
sentences.zh: 闵采尔只是搭了农民起义的顺风车。

sentences.en: But I think he does matter because he is a foretaste of the radicalism that you're talking about.
sentences.zh: 但我认为他确实很重要，因为他是你所说的激进主义的先声。

sentences.en: So, you know, the belief that you can only understand scripture if you are possessed by the spirit.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，那种认为只有被圣灵附体才能理解经文的信念，

sentences.en: I mean, this is fundamental to Baptists and Quakers and Anabaptists and all these kinds of people who will be emerging from this kind of forging ground.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这对浸信会、贵格会、再洗礼派以及所有这些将从这片熔炉中涌现出来的群体来说，都是根本性的。

sentences.en: So in terms of the war itself, Munzer is not important.
sentences.zh: 所以就战争本身而言，闵采尔并不重要。

sentences.en: But as a kind of portent of what will come, I think he is important.
sentences.zh: 但作为一种未来趋势的预兆，我认为他很重要。

sentences.en: And you're right that Luther does focus on him.
sentences.zh: 你说得对，路德确实把焦点对准了他。

sentences.en: And just as Munzer had seen the hand of the devil in the victory of the princes, Luther sees the hand of the devil in the entire conflict.
sentences.zh: 正如闵采尔在诸侯的胜利中看到了魔鬼之手，路德也在整场冲突中看到了魔鬼之手。

sentences.en: And it's not just the destruction.
sentences.zh: 而且不仅仅是破坏。

sentences.en: So you have, you know, 100,000 people slaughtered.
sentences.zh: 你知道，有10万人被屠杀。

sentences.en: I mean, terrible bloodletting.
sentences.zh: 我是说，可怕的流血事件。

sentences.en: It's also that Luther is being blamed for this bloodshed by lots of his enemies.
sentences.zh: 而且路德也因为这场流血事件被他的许多敌人指责。

sentences.en: So here is Johann Cocleus, the guy who had argued with him at Verbs and the subject of all those very abusive pictures.
sentences.zh: 这就是约翰·科克莱乌斯，那个曾在沃尔姆斯与他争论过的人，也是那些极具侮辱性的图片的主角。

sentences.en: Cocleus wrote, there were many peasants slain in the uprising, many fanatics banished, many false prophets hanged,
sentences.zh: 科克莱乌斯写道：起义中有许多农民被杀，许多狂热分子被流放，许多假先知被绞死、

sentences.en: burned, drowned, or beheaded, who perhaps would still live as good, obedient Christians had he never written.
sentences.zh: 烧死、淹死或斩首，如果他从未写过那些东西，这些人或许还能作为善良、顺从的基督徒活着。

sentences.en: And I think it's a mark of how unsettling this charge is to Luther, as well as of his complete
sentences.zh: 我认为，路德将农民战争视为魔鬼直接试图摧毁他的一次尝试，这既标志着这种指控对他来说有多么不安，也标志着他完全的

sentences.en: egocentrism, that he sees the peasants' war as a direct attempt by the devil to destroy him.
sentences.zh: 自我中心。

sentences.en: It's all about me.
sentences.zh: 一切都围绕着我。

sentences.en: It really is all about Luther.
sentences.zh: 确实，一切都围绕着路德。

sentences.en: So his response to this is twofold.
sentences.zh: 所以他对此的回应是双重的。

sentences.en: The first is very personal.
sentences.zh: 第一点是非常个人的。

sentences.en: The second is much more public.
sentences.zh: 第二点则要公开得多。

sentences.en: So the first thing he does, Munzer has been accusing him of being a monk, of being a pope, and so on.
sentences.zh: 他做的第一件事是，闵采尔一直指责他是个修士、是个教皇等等。

sentences.en: So he responds to this in the most provocative way that he can.
sentences.zh: 所以他以最挑衅的方式回应了这一点。

sentences.en: So on the 13th of June, 1525, a month after the death of Munzer, Luther marries a nun.
sentences.zh: 1525年6月13日，在闵采尔死后一个月，路德娶了一位修女。

sentences.en: And this is a woman called
sentences.zh: 这位女性名叫

sentences.en: Katerina von Bora, who is 26.
sentences.zh: 卡塔琳娜·冯·博拉，她当时26岁。

sentences.en: So he's not doing a Karlstadt.
sentences.zh: 所以他没有像卡尔施塔特那样。

sentences.en: How old is he?
sentences.zh: 他多大岁数了？

sentences.en: He's in his early 40s by this point.
sentences.zh: 他当时已经四十出头了。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So he's done well for himself, but he hasn't completely embarrassed himself.
sentences.zh: 所以他做得不错，但也没有让自己彻底丢脸。

sentences.en: He hasn't gotten the full Leo.
sentences.zh: 他没有完全像利奥那样。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So he'd actually played a part in helping her to escape from her convent.
sentences.zh: 实际上，他在帮助她逃离修道院的过程中发挥了作用。

sentences.en: She'd read him and become an evangelical, wanted to leave the nunnery that she'd been in.
sentences.zh: 她读过他的著作并成为了福音派信徒，想要离开她所在的修女院。

sentences.en: And Luther arranges for her to escape in a wagon carrying barrels of herring.
sentences.zh: 路德安排她藏在一辆装满鲱鱼桶的马车里逃了出来。

sentences.en: And she seems great.
sentences.zh: 她看起来很棒。

sentences.en: You know, she's kind of funny, smart, good for Luther, I think.
sentences.zh: 你知道，她挺风趣、聪明，我认为这对路德很有好处。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And Luther claimed that he had married her to please his father, annoy the pope, amuse the angels, and make the devil weep.
sentences.zh: 路德声称他娶她是为了取悦他的父亲、惹恼教皇、逗乐天使，并让魔鬼哭泣。

sentences.en: But he is happy with her.
sentences.zh: 但他确实和她在一起很幸福。

sentences.en: Obviously, I mean, he's a massive patriarch.
sentences.zh: 显然，我是说，他是个大男子主义者。

sentences.en: He's in no way a feminist dad, I think it would be fair to say.
sentences.zh: 公平地说，他绝不是一个女权主义父亲。

sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But they get on well.
sentences.zh: 但他们相处得很好。

sentences.zh: 她为他生了六个孩子。

sentences.zh: 她还帮他变得更胖了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I think he's quite a fun father.
sentences.zh: 而且我觉得他是个挺有趣的父亲。

sentences.en: So he says to his infant son, become a lawyer and I'll hang you.
sentences.zh: 他曾对年幼的儿子说：去当律师吧，我就把你吊死。

sentences.en: I've said that to my son.
sentences.zh: 我也对我儿子说过这话。

sentences.en: I think that's good paternal advice, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我觉得这是很好的父亲建议，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Never be alone.
sentences.zh: 不要孤身一人。

sentences.en: Act foolish and play.
sentences.zh: 尽情玩乐，举止随性。

sentences.en: Drink a lot.
sentences.zh: 多喝点酒。

sentences.en: It would even be a good idea to commit a sin, but not a gross one.
sentences.zh: 甚至犯点小错也无妨，只要别太过分就行。

sentences.en: That's how he advises his children to avoid depression.
sentences.zh: 这就是他建议孩子们如何避免抑郁的方法。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's good advice.
sentences.zh: 没错，这建议不错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Have a bit of fun, but don't go too far.
sentences.zh: 找点乐子，但别玩过火。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错，正是如此。

sentences.en: And I think that all of this is kind of an expression of what we were talking about before, how because Luther sees all humans as irredeemably steeped in sin,
sentences.zh: 我认为这一切其实都是我们之前所谈论内容的体现，因为路德认为全人类都无可救药地沉溺于罪恶之中，

sentences.en: well, irredeemably, unless God, of course, does choose to redeem them, to allow them to be born again.
sentences.zh: 嗯，除非上帝选择救赎他们，让他们获得重生，否则就是无可救药的。

sentences.en: In a sense, it doesn't really matter.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，这其实并不重要。

sentences.en: You're not going to get closer to heaven by being a killjoy, celebrate all your life.
sentences.zh: 做一个扫兴的人并不会让你离天堂更近，尽情享受你的人生吧。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Tom, he's gone back up on my estimation because that seems like a very sane and healthy view.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我对他的评价又回升了，因为这看起来是一个非常理智且健康的观点。

sentences.en: We're all damned, unless God, of course, redeems us.
sentences.zh: 我们都是罪人，除非上帝救赎我们。

sentences.en: We're all weak and feeble.
sentences.zh: 我们都是软弱无力的。

sentences.en: Don't beat yourself up about having a night on the town.
sentences.zh: 别因为出去狂欢了一晚就自责不已。

sentences.en: That's basically his attitude, is it?
sentences.zh: 他基本上就是这个态度，对吧？

sentences.en: Not exactly, but I think he thinks that certainly when it comes to marrying, you might as well.
sentences.zh: 不完全是，但我认为他确实觉得在结婚这件事上，你最好还是结了。

sentences.en: I mean, you're not going to get any closer to heaven by not marrying.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，不结婚并不会让你离天堂更近。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So that's put Luther in a good light, perhaps, by your standards.
sentences.zh: 所以按照你的标准，这或许让路德显得还不错。

sentences.en: But now we come to the more splenetic ways in which Luther responds to the Peasants' Revolt.
sentences.zh: 但现在我们来看看路德在应对农民起义时表现出的那种暴躁一面。

sentences.en: So the couple of months before the Battle of Frankenhausen, so when the war is at its most vicious in Saxony and Thuringia.
sentences.zh: 在弗兰肯豪森战役前的几个月里，也就是战争在萨克森和图林根最惨烈的时候。

sentences.en: Luther goes on a tour of Thuringia, kind of preaching to all the rebellious peasants, all the rebellious miners, and is very, very unsettled by it.
sentences.zh: 路德去图林根巡回演讲，向所有反叛的农民和矿工布道，他对此感到非常非常不安。

sentences.en: In May, he publishes a pamphlet that to this day remains very controversial, absolutely ensured that he would not feature on
sentences.zh: 五月，他发表了一本至今仍极具争议的小册子，这绝对确保了他不会出现在

sentences.en: East German banknotes.
sentences.zh: 东德的钞票上。

sentences.en: And this is a pamphlet called Against the Robbing and the Murdering
sentences.zh: 这本小册子名为《反对杀人越货的农民暴徒》，

sentences.en: Hordes of Peasants, which is a very Daily Telegraph kind of headline.
sentences.zh: 这标题很有《每日电讯报》的风格。

sentences.en: It is very, I was just thinking the Daily Telegraph would love that.
sentences.zh: 确实，我刚才就在想《每日电讯报》会喜欢这个标题。

sentences.en: So he'd actually published an earlier pamphlet in which he'd been more ambivalent, kind of basically saying the peasants and princes are both awful, just stop it.
sentences.zh: 他其实早先发表过一本小册子，态度比较暧昧，基本上是说农民和诸侯都很糟糕，让他们停手。

sentences.en: But now he gives the rebels both barrels.
sentences.zh: 但现在，他火力全开地抨击叛军。

sentences.en: So I think there is not a devil left in hell, he writes.
sentences.zh: 他写道，我想地狱里已经没有魔鬼了。

sentences.en: They have all gone into the peasants.
sentences.zh: 它们全都钻进农民身体里了。

sentences.en: And then he urges in this very, very notorious phrase, stab, smite, slay whoever you can.
sentences.zh: 然后他在那句臭名昭著的话中敦促道：刺杀、击打、屠戮，尽你所能。

sentences.en: And that is directed at the princes.
sentences.zh: 这话是针对诸侯说的。

sentences.en: And many, many of his admirers are appalled.
sentences.zh: 他的许多崇拜者都感到震惊。

sentences.en: But Luther never repents it.
sentences.zh: 但路德从未忏悔。

sentences.en: He never regrets it.
sentences.zh: 他从未后悔。

sentences.en: I mean, he does condemn atrocities against the peasants.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他确实谴责了针对农民的暴行。

sentences.en: So Munzer's wife is raped after the Battle of Frankenhausen, and he condemns that very, very firmly.
sentences.zh: 比如闵采尔的妻子在弗兰肯豪森战役后被强奸，他对此进行了非常严厉的谴责。

sentences.en: He condemns the blinding of 60 peasants who supposedly had failed to look at a Lutheran lord in a respectful manner.
sentences.zh: 他谴责了对60名农民施以剜眼之刑，仅仅因为他们被认为没有以恭敬的态度对待一位路德派领主。

sentences.en: But despite these atrocities, he continues to feel that divine justice has prevailed.
sentences.zh: 但尽管有这些暴行，他依然觉得这是神圣正义的胜利。

sentences.en: And that is expressive of this inner dread of the devil that has been with him all the way through, and of his hatred for the agents of the devil.
sentences.zh: 这表达了他内心深处一直以来对魔鬼的恐惧，以及他对魔鬼代理人的憎恨。

sentences.en: And we talked about the relish he has for violence in his language.
sentences.zh: 我们谈到过他在语言中对暴力的那种嗜好。

sentences.en: I think there is a relish for violence when it is targeted against people who he sees as the devil's agents.
sentences.zh: 我认为当暴力针对他眼中魔鬼的代理人时，他确实有一种嗜好。

sentences.en: And it's this, Tom, psychologically, because ultimately Luther is quite conservative.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，从心理学角度看，这是因为路德本质上相当保守。

sentences.en: Yeah, he is.
sentences.zh: 没错，他是。

sentences.en: I mean, he's from a fairly upwardly mobile, respectable background.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他出身于一个相当向上流动、体面的背景。

sentences.en: Although he likes going against the authority of the institutions that he's in, the university, the church, whatever.
sentences.zh: 尽管他喜欢反抗他所处的机构权威，比如大学、教会等等。

sentences.en: Ultimately, he doesn't want to see the social order turned upside down.
sentences.zh: 但归根结底，他不想看到社会秩序被颠覆。

sentences.en: He doesn't want to live in a millenarian paradise.
sentences.zh: 他不想生活在千禧年主义的乐园里。

sentences.en: I think he, I mean, he's owed everything to the elector, the figure of the elector, Frederick.
sentences.zh: 我认为他，我的意思是，他的一切都归功于选帝侯，也就是弗雷德里克选帝侯。

sentences.en: Of course, yeah.
sentences.zh: 当然，没错。

sentences.en: And there's no reason why he would regard the overthrow of that regime as being something that God would want.
sentences.zh: 而且没有理由认为他会把推翻那个政权视为上帝的旨意。

sentences.en: I think it's different, say, if you are being raised in a Swiss city.
sentences.zh: 我想如果你是在瑞士城市长大的，情况就不同了。

sentences.en: Because as you said, then the scope for envisaging a different social order is much greater.
sentences.zh: 因为正如你所说，那样的话，构想不同社会秩序的空间要大得多。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: But I think it's also expressive of a dread that disorder is the devil's way of trying to overthrow everything that Luther is doing.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这也表达了一种恐惧，即混乱是魔鬼试图推翻路德所做一切的手段。

sentences.en: And I think that's sharpened by probably, I mean, I don't want to over-psychologize it, but the fact that Luther himself has precipitated
sentences.zh: 我认为这一点可能被加剧了，我的意思是，我不想过度心理分析，但路德本人引发了

sentences.en: this great ruction perhaps means that he is, you know, there's a bit of displacement going on.
sentences.zh: 这场巨大的动荡，或许意味着他，你知道，存在某种心理投射。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's certainly that sense that people who resemble him, who are the particular targets
sentences.zh: 这肯定是一种感觉，即那些与他相似的人，也就是他仇恨的特定目标，

sentences.en: of his hatred, and actually the most notorious example of this isn't the peasants, but the Jews.
sentences.zh: 实际上，这方面最臭名昭著的例子不是农民，而是犹太人。

sentences.en: And even more notorious than the pamphlet he writes against the peasants is a pamphlet he writes just
sentences.zh: 比他那本反对农民的小册子更臭名昭著的，是他去世前三年，即1546年去世，

sentences.en: three years before his death in 1546, so it comes out in 1543, called On the Jews and their lies.
sentences.zh: 这本小册子出版于1543年，名为《论犹太人及其谎言》。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I wonder if we can answer this.
sentences.zh: 我想知道我们能否回答这个问题。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So, I mean, we can't talk about Luther and not discuss this because in the episode we
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们不能不讨论路德的这一点，因为在我们做的那期关于纽伦堡集会的节目中，

sentences.en: did on the Nuremberg rallies, we talked about how at the 1934 Nuremberg rally, a copy of this pamphlet was on display.
sentences.zh: 我们谈到了1934年纽伦堡集会上，这本小册子的副本是如何被展示出来的。

sentences.en: And the language is terrible.
sentences.zh: 而且语言非常可怕。

sentences.en: So you have all his customary cloacal obsessions.
sentences.zh: 他充满了惯有的排泄物式的执念。

sentences.en: So he says of the Jews, and by this point, I think people who've made it this far will recognize the authentic Lutheran touch in this.
sentences.zh: 所以他谈到犹太人时说——我想听到这里的听众会认出这是典型的路德式风格——

sentences.en: The devil stuffs and squirts the Jews so full that it overflows and swims out of every place.
sentences.zh: 魔鬼把犹太人塞得满满当当，以至于污秽溢出，从每一个地方流出来。

sentences.en: Pure devil's filth.
sentences.zh: 纯粹的魔鬼污秽。

sentences.en: Yes, it tastes so good to their hearts and they guzzle it like sows.
sentences.zh: 是的，这对他们的心来说味道好极了，他们像母猪一样大口吞咽。

sentences.en: So that's shocking enough.
sentences.zh: 这已经够令人震惊了。

sentences.en: But what's really shocking are the things that Luther demands should be done to the Jews.
sentences.zh: 但真正令人震惊的是路德要求对犹太人采取的行动。

sentences.en: I mean, Luther is writing, of course, before the HolocauSt. But even so, when you read the pamphlet and you read Luther's demands that
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，路德写这些的时候当然是在大屠杀之前。但即便如此，当你读到这本小册子，读到路德要求

sentences.en: the Jews be rounded up, that they all be housed in one place beneath a single roof, that they be put
sentences.zh: 将犹太人围捕起来，把他们全部安置在同一个屋檐下，让他们从事

sentences.en: to hard labor, that the Talmud, their scriptures, their synagogues should be burnt.
sentences.zh: 苦役，烧毁《塔木德》、他们的经文和犹太会堂时，

sentences.zh: 然后，引用路德的话，烧不掉的就埋起来，盖上土，这样就再也没有人能看到他们哪怕一块石头或灰烬了。

sentences.en: I mean, it is chilling.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这令人不寒而栗。

sentences.en: And the Nazis loved this, right?
sentences.zh: 纳粹很喜欢这个，对吧？

sentences.en: The Nazis embraced Luther as one of their own.
sentences.zh: 纳粹把路德视为他们自己人。

sentences.en: Yeah, of course.
sentences.zh: 是的，当然。

sentences.en: And I think it's doubly disturbing for admirers of Luther, both because, I mean, this is shocking even by the standards of the time.
sentences.zh: 我认为这对路德的崇拜者来说是双重困扰，因为即便以当时的眼光来看，这也令人震惊。

sentences.en: As with the peasants, people who admire
sentences.zh: 和对待农民一样，那些崇拜路德的人

sentences.en: Luther are really appalled to read this.
sentences.zh: 读到这些时真的感到震惊。

sentences.en: They kind of think he's really gone too far with this.
sentences.zh: 他们觉得他在这件事上真的做得太过分了。

sentences.en: And the other thing that's disturbing about it is that it's not just a rehashing of anti-Semitism.
sentences.zh: 另一件令人不安的事情是，这不仅仅是反犹主义的重弹旧调。

sentences.en: So basically, what precipitates this is Luther's feeling that it is those who have been granted rebirth by God.
sentences.zh: 基本上，导致这一切的是路德的一种感觉，即那些被上帝赋予重生的人，

sentences.en: So we could probably call them Protestants now, without risk of anachronism, because that word is starting to be used by the time Luther writes this pamphlet, that they are God's
sentences.zh: 所以我们现在大概可以称他们为新教徒，而不必担心时代错误，因为路德写这本小册子时这个词已经开始被使用了，他们是上帝的

sentences.en: chosen people.
sentences.zh: 选民。

sentences.en: And that, therefore, the Jews claiming to be God's chosen people, that it's you know, it's cast by Luther as a stupidity and folly and arrogance.
sentences.zh: 因此，犹太人自称是上帝的选民，这在路德看来是一种愚蠢、荒唐和傲慢。

sentences.en: So that idea of we have been chosen and they are our antithesis because they rejected the word.
sentences.zh: 所以那种“我们是选民，而他们因为拒绝了圣言，所以是我们的对立面”的想法。

sentences.en: I mean, that you could, if you were being harsh to Luther, you could say, well, doesn't that very
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你对路德严苛一点，你可以说，这难道不是非常

sentences.zh: 清晰地预示了你在那期精彩的关于纳粹意识形态的节目中谈到的纳粹思想吗？

sentences.en: Nazi ideology?
sentences.zh: 那种他们被自然选择为超人的想法？

sentences.en: The idea that they have been chosen by nature to be the supermen.
sentences.zh: 他们是开明的人。

sentences.en: They are the enlightened ones.
sentences.zh: 他们是高贵和人类精神以及一切美好事物的代表。而纳粹认为犹太人是他们完全的、兽性的对立面。

sentences.en: They are the representatives of nobility and the human spirit and all that is beSt. And the Nazis believed that the Jews were their complete sort of bestial antithesis.
sentences.zh: 路德现在说的就是这个意思。

sentences.en: That's kind of what Luther is saying right now.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 他谈的不是自然。

sentences.zh: 他谈的是上帝，但他认为新教徒是选民，而犹太人是反面。

sentences.zh: 这就是纳粹所做的事情。

sentences.en: Okay.

sentences.zh: 所以这是基于神学而非种族。

sentences.en: So it is theologically based rather than racially based.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我相信这对犹太听众来说没什么安慰作用。

sentences.en: I mean, I'm sure that's not much comfort to Jewish listeners.
sentences.zh: 但汤姆，这种二分法的观念，这种“我们与他们”的观念，即犹太人是终极恶棍。

sentences.en: But Tom, the idea of a dichotomy, the idea of this kind of us and them, that the Jews are the supreme villains.
sentences.zh: 他们不是终极恶棍。

sentences.en: They're not the supreme villains.
